name: schema-org-thing

schema.description: This is a JSON schema representation of the schema.org Thing schema: https://schema.org/Thing

@context.description: override the @context property to ensure the schema.org URI is used

additionalType.description: An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. In RDFa syntax, it is better to use the native RDFa syntax - the 'typeof' attribute - for multiple types. Schema.org tools may have only weaker understanding of extra types, in particular those defined externally.

disambiguatingDescription.description: A sub property of description. A short description of the item used to disambiguate from other, similar items. Information from other properties (in particular, name) may be necessary for the description to be useful for disambiguation.

image.description: An image of the item. This can be a URL or a fully described ImageObject.

mainEntityOfPage.description: Indicates a page (or other CreativeWork) for which this thing is the main entity being described. See background notes for details. Inverse property mainEntity.

potentialAction.description: Indicates a potential Action, which describes an idealized action in which this thing would play an 'object' role.

sameAs.description: URL of a reference Web page that unambiguously indicates the item's identity. E.g. the URL of the item's Wikipedia page, Freebase page, or official website.

schema.title: JSON schema for schema.org / Thing

erroneous_json.description: English mathematician and writer, known for her work on Charles Babbage's early mechanical general-purpose computer, the Analytical Engine.

valid_json.name: Ada Lovelace
valid_json.description: English mathematician and writer, known for her work on Charles Babbage's early mechanical general-purpose computer, the Analytical Engine.

description:
Ada Lovelace, also known by her alternate name Augusta Ada King, was an English mathematician and writer best remembered for her pioneering work on Charles Babbage’s early mechanical general‑purpose computer, the Analytical Engine. She is a 19th‑century mathematician and early computer programmer, a distinction highlighted in her disambiguating description. Detailed information about her can be found on her Wikipedia page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ada_Lovelace) and her Wikidata entry (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q7251). In addition to being classified as a Person, she is also identified as a Historical Figure via the external type https://example.org/vocab#HistoricalFigure.

A portrait of Ada Lovelace is available at https://example.com/images/ada.jpg, captioned “Portrait of Ada Lovelace.” The article https://example.org/articles/ada-lovelace treats her as the main entity of the page. For further exploration, a built‑in SearchAction allows users to query the site with a required search term; the target URL is https://example.org/search?q={search_term_string}, where the query input must be provided as search_term_string.
